column8: Mon 16 Nov: 2.3/3e scale only; check slide 81 first: the overall median $12,000 sits above the 5th decile's $10,000, impossible if both are medians of one group; never size her income from it (claim 5).

Mon 16 Nov: 3e career test: the one set where the US top fell more than the middle; say two cross-sections five years apart, not a Covid-year measure, and check what the overall median refers to (deciles 2-5 fell while it rose 20%).
Mon 16 Nov: guard for 2.3: inside the top tenth incomes span about 100 times, so no decile sizes her year; the source conflicts on the floor ($83,400 or $84,200), so cite neither.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e area (2) and Table 3 row 1: a zero book year is common among full-time US authors; pairs with Q56-005, and one of the two is enough in prose.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e area (2) and Table 3 row 1: work in print every year and still a zero year, so the deposit is confirmed by 1 Dec 2027 and nothing is stated before it lands; say UK writers of all kinds, not authors like her.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 lumpiness: about 2 in 5 UK authors doubled or halved their writing income over 2008-13, so the swing is personal as much as the cycle; recall data and Keel arithmetic, said so.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q1-039 (concentration of UK author income at the top); adds the 2012/13 point (58%, Gini 0.69) to its series.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.3/3e support: UK lecture income is very skewed (mean 2,714 pounds, median 250); it does not show top authors are the ones who earn it, so say only that speaking money goes to a few.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 and 3e career test: in 2020 the UK 80th percentile held (+2% real) while the 20th fell 16%; replaces SKELETON's 'the link is strong for top earners' for authors. CLASH RISK: qualifies IPS l.9's 'later and smaller' for top earnings in 2020 (IPS frozen; 3e already says 2009 supports it, 2020 does not); say top fifth and all-source earnings.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e support for Q56-009: agented UK authors' writing median held at 10,000 pounds nominal in both years; an agent is a rough proxy, so a clause at most.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e support: Australia's share above A$200,000 rose from 2.5% to 5.3% between surveys seven years apart; nominal threshold and all-source income, so a weak second country beside Q56-009.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3/3e: Australian children's authors' practice income rose while events fell; the case never says her books are children's, so use only as which streams held and which fell, never as her income.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q1-037 (the typical author's long slide is a trend, not the cycle); Canada adds a third country, store only.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e career test: the Forbes top ten without Rowling barely moved between the years to June 2008 and June 2010; say before and after, never through, since the worst year (to June 2009) is missing, and check $270m less Rowling's $10m is $260m (-1.1%), not $259m (-1.5%).
Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 lumpiness: at the very top one author's own calendar moved a year's income -97% to +40% while the group barely moved; Forbes estimates and famous outliers, so one clause.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.3/3e: 96% of a fiction bestseller's sales come in its first year, so an author's year depends on whether a book came out; verified network science; cash follows contract dates (Q12).

Mon 16 Nov: guard for 2.3 and 3d: one week on the list makes a bestselling author for life, so the case's 'bestselling' never sizes her income or decile; a rule for the writers, not a claim about her.

Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q12-006 (2009 advance cuts fell on the midlist, not proven names); The Bookseller adds forecasts by an agent and an editor, not outcomes, and Q1-030's cut to a quarter runs the other way.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3/3e: in 2020 deal counts rose (+8%, read at source) while $500,000+ deals fell 17% (read only in a blog's copy); read Publishers Lunch at source or say 'softened' as Q12-007 does; the fall began in 2019.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: six-figure children's graphic-novel deals 3, 10, 24 (blog copy, unverified); the case never says her books are children's, so never 'her corner of the market'.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e recovery: US deal counts were up 19% on 2020 by April 2021, so the advance stream came back in about a year; counts, not sums, and a secondary report.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.3/3e: the share of speakers at $500,000 or more fell from 7% to 4% in 2020, the top's clearest fall; self-selected speakers, not authors; adds the top to Q12b-012.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e recovery by stream: the speaking top recovered first while cancellations ran 20-30% of gigs in 2021; store only, Q56-036 carries it.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q12b-012 (speaking took two to three years to come back); event attendance at 57-68% of 2019 into mid-2022 adds a measure; the Forbes line was read only in an excerpt.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: speaking falls through bookings more than fees in a recession; an undated press release on motivational speakers, never cited for her.

Mon 16 Nov: store only: US physical book exports -14.6% and imports -25.9% in H1 2009; it measures physical trade, not rights, so drop 'foreign editions and rights are the likelier casualty' unless a rights figure is found.

Mon 16 Nov: store only, residency context: Taiwan's book publishers' revenue fell about 31% in 2016-23 (Keel arithmetic), a trend, not a cycle; the link to co-sponsors is untested and the 2021-22 step may be a reporting break.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: in Taiwan's 2020 new books sold more while backlist and fairs fell; Taiwan-language publisher revenue serves no part on its own.
Mon 16 Nov: store only, a method note: Taiwan's statistics cannot see an author's income, so 3e rests the career idea on US, UK and Australian data, as it already does.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 or 3e: UK law lets creators average two years when one is under 75% of the other, an outside institution writing lumpiness into law; say the law expects swings of a quarter or more; UK law, not hers.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q56-030 (tax law averages creators' lumpy income); Australia makes it two countries in one clause of Q56-030's use.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e limit: every statement about the top compares different people at two dates; one clause if the report leans on Q56-009 or Q56-014.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 and 3e: at the top the cycle ran through speaking and the biggest advances, not book income, which narrows IPS l.9 to its own words ('the speaking fees', 'advances'). CLASH RISK: top book income held in 2020, so never say all her income falls; leans on unverified Q56-019.

Mon 16 Nov: guard for 3e area (2): the case puts her living costs outside the portfolio but gives neither the costs nor what is already earned, so an income fall never converts into a deposit forecast; corrects Q12b-019, which took costs out of the deposit.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e area (2) and Table 3 row 1: measured falls at the top sit far below the 74.5% cut the escrow standard survives (NUMBERS 5); lead with the plan's own standard (the first $38,282, 25.5%) and give the $2,388 top-up only as at forward rates, never 'the payments need only 1.6%'; row 19's -17% unverified.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e recovery by stream: books and deals back in about a year, paid appearances in two to three; a downturn reaches the 2028 deposit only if it starts by 2027 (Q12b-018).

Mon 16 Nov: 3e context only: $150,000 is more than the UK top tenth's entry income; never imply her decile or income (claim 5), and say 'nothing is stated before it lands', not 'never leans on it', since the top-up and extra Treasuries come from it first.

Mon 16 Nov: lineage for the ladder (2.0 or 3a): Roy's own yardstick gives money a zero standard error in money terms, so the Treasury paying the dollar sum on its date is his zero-error asset; Roy wrote about borrowing, so the mapping is Keel's, said so.

Mon 16 Nov: lineage for the ladder: Roy in 1952 warned a ten-year scheme off short funding because of the rate on reborrowing, the case for matching dates; he writes as a borrower and Laura is the lender, so say the same logic, not the same case.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q13-008 (only one path happens, so the average is irrelevant); Roy (1952) is the older source and can join its citation.
Mon 16 Nov: lineage for the 2031 move (3c): Roy's ambush line; the move is a dated trade before the meetings, never a rule that reacts to prices (Q3a).

Mon 16 Nov: store or 3e: Roy counts inflation as a disaster (70% is his example); fix 'not the dollar payments': inflation cannot leave a payment short of its dollars but does lower what each buys (H4-048); her flexibility is a cushion, never a hedge.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 lineage: Roy makes diversification the safety of the wealthier, money with room above the disaster level, which backs aha 2 (spread only what is not promised); the promised and unpromised mapping is Keel inference.
Mon 16 Nov: lineage exhibit: safety-first came from insurers' ruin theory (Roy's footnote to Cramer), insurers meeting fixed claims as Laura meets ten; Cramer not read, so cite Roy only.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.0 or lineage: Markowitz gives Roy an equal share of MPT's honour; Markowitz (1999) unread, so cite it as quoted in Rubinstein (2002) in APA's secondary form, or read FAJ 55(4) first.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of H3-019 (Markowitz 1952 is one period, used only inside VT); Chhabra's 'diversified as prescribed by MPT' can join its sources.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 and the lineage exhibit (EXPECTATIONS 2.4): BPT says layered investors hold bonds plus lottery tickets; Caplet keeps the layers and fills them with the CAPM's two funds; pairs with Q57-042 and Q57-011; goes past H3-025.

Mon 16 Nov: central idea's lineage (2.3): BPT investors overlook covariances and Caplet's layers exist because of one. CLASH RISK: the covariance is IPS l.9's, which Q56-009 and Q56-033 qualify for top book income in 2020; say 'in the same downturn' (3e).

Mon 16 Nov: store or the lineage exhibit's refused cell: BPT predicts demand for floor-plus-index notes; the plan has that shape with no note, issuer or option; never call it a note, capital-protected or portfolio insurance (it is buy-and-hold); near H2-068.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c lineage: the range rule as Kataoka's criterion; Kataoka unread, so cite via Shefrin and Statman; say alpha near zero, not zero, since an iBond fund pays net asset value, and give the bottom as the floor's zero-interest payout less 0.5%, rounded down ($98,380 to $95,000), never 'what the floor pays'.
Mon 16 Nov: References and lineage order: Roy, then Kataoka, Telser, Arzac and Bawa, Lopes, then BPT; only Roy and Shefrin and Statman were read, so the rest are cited through them.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 and 3.0, the central idea's lineage: Chhabra's aspirational bucket holds a business tied to one's own income, so her career is that bucket and the portfolio adds none; settles H3-027 against H7-099; answer his s9.9 (earning power as personal risk) in the same breath.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a support: Chhabra's 'the journey matters' is the sequence point H2-006 and H1-002 make; the ladder takes the path away from the payments; one clause at most.
Mon 16 Nov: lineage exhibit's refused cell: Chhabra builds his buckets with puts and calls, Caplet with owned Treasuries and one index fund (derivatives are banned in WInS).
Mon 16 Nov: lineage for the half kept and the order of claims (3b): Brunel's least important goal bears the most residual risk; a practitioner's line for H7-015.

Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 or 3b: Brunel's philanthropic goals take the least risk and losses fall elsewhere; fix 'any loss falls on the half kept' to 'after the 2031 move', since before it a fall lowers the top she can state.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 support: Wilcox's ratio ties risk to discretionary wealth, and VT is 6.63% of the $450,000 (NUMBERS 8g); Wilcox unread and Caplet sized VT as the remainder, so never as the method and never beside a textbook share.
Mon 16 Nov: presentation: risk as dollars short on a date, not volatility (Pfau on Bodie and Taqqu; JFP 2014); cite Pfau, since the book was not read; near H9-038.

Mon 16 Nov: store, a judge's question: a surplus is not automatic risk appetite; the IPS's answer is that the half kept is promised to no one and is her flexibility; a journalist's paraphrase, never quoted as Brunel's words.
Mon 16 Nov: lineage for the ladder and floor: Zwecher's floor is a subportfolio of safe, time-dated cash flows; read in the publisher's preview, it upgrades H5-067 (unverified).

Mon 16 Nov: lineage exhibit's refused cell: Zwecher puts only wealth above the floor's cost at risk and re-sizes as wealth moves; VT's $29,829 is the remainder bought once (NUMBERS 4); never present the plan as his rule (buy-and-hold, Q3a).
Mon 16 Nov: lineage for the 2028 completion: Zwecher's underfunded floor and 'Raising the Floor' (chapter titles only); call it the ladder, not 'the floor', which in the report is the 2032 fund.
Mon 16 Nov: lineage for the 2031 move and the conceit: at-risk flooring (pencil) becomes locked-in flooring (ink); search excerpt only, so fetch Pfau's June 2012 piece before use.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b support: an owned floor frees the upside to sit through a crash; an interview, secondary; 'one whack at the cat' echoes Q13-008.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c lineage for the 2031 move: Merton takes risk out once the goal is achieved; a parallel in aim only, since his rule runs on funded status and Caplet's is one dated trade (buy-and-hold, Q3a), never a trigger.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e and Table 3's market-price row: Merton says floor-value rules would bar long Treasuries, the safest assets for dated income; backs TNA note 2 and H7-003.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d and Table 3: hedging income makes capital value swing, so communication matters; Table 3 watches what each holding pays and the co-sponsor words say so.

Mon 16 Nov: lineage for the reserve from 2033: Merton's ladder category does his guaranteed-income job for Laura's dollar payments. CLASH RISK (recorded): his ladder spends interest as income; never imply later bonds' interest pays earlier payments.
Mon 16 Nov: lineage exhibit's refused cell: Merton copies an annuity that cannot be bought by trading; Laura buys dated Treasuries outright and holds them; TIPS only as his tool, never hers.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q1c-023 and H3-028 (riskier earnings, fewer shares); Bodie and Clowes is the personal-finance entry for the central idea's lineage, one citation at most beside BMS.
Mon 16 Nov: lineage for the 2028 completion: price the goal with no risk first, then choose risk; near H3-001; the mapping is Keel inference.

Mon 16 Nov: store or lineage: Bodie's reversal is that shares are risky in the long run (Q39-017), the IPS's that her career is already shares; say they reverse different wisdoms, never 'the same reversal'.
Mon 16 Nov: 2031 move lineage: payments locked now (Bodie and Taqqu, via Pfau) and the range later (Pfau); the book and Guyton's survey unread, so cite Pfau's review and drop Guyton.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a lineage: Sharpe's sealed box per year is the ladder and the facility box is opened once before 2031; a citation in the lineage exhibit, never a second image beside pencil and ink.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.0 and 3.0 naming: the Sharpe of Perold and Sharpe left dynamic strategies out of his own retirement design on purpose and chose buy-and-hold boxes; backs Q3a-034's buy-and-hold.

Mon 16 Nov: store or a note: a safe asset plus the market gives a straight line in market return; fix 'no kink': the contribution is capped at the stated top, so only the floor-plus-shares holding is linear; utility language too hard for the prose.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e and the two reasons: 'you still have the key'; Laura's only keys are written down, a missed deposit or a Treasury default; an interview, secondary.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a and 3f (aha 10): a fixed spending plan funded by a volatile portfolio is 'fundamentally flawed'; the academic source H1-002 and H2-006 lack; their case is 30 years of real spending.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 and the lineage exhibit: with dated liabilities the risk-free asset is the liability-matching portfolio, and with a world market portfolio it forms a new two-fund theorem, Caplet's ladder and floor plus VT; upgrades H3-020 (Tobin's cash); body unread, so quote the abstract.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e, nominal not real: 'nominal if protecting nominal consumption' answers why not inflation-linked bonds on principle (TIPS are also banned this year); working-paper text, check the FAJ version.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c: an aspirational liability cannot be made risk-free by investing alone, only by buying it, which is why the top is stated only once owned; the payments are not ARVA, which cuts spending with the portfolio.

Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 and 3c: safety-first counts the whole household balance sheet (her career), and in Kitces's terms the payments' risk is transferred in 2027 and the range's in 2031; the JFP page shows no author.
